translations.text: And King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom.
And Daniel was a companion of the king, and was honoured above all his friends.
And the Babylonians had an idol whose name was Bel; and every day there were given to it twelve measures (griv) of fine flour, forty sheep, and six measures of wine.
And the king served it, and went every day to worship it; but Daniel worshipped his own God. The king said to him, "Why do you not worship Bel?"
And Daniel said to him, "Because I do not worship an idol made with hands, but the living God, who made heaven and earth and has dominion over all flesh."
The king said to him, "And now, do you not think that Bel is a living god? Or do you not see how much he eats and drinks every day?"
Daniel laughed and said to him, "Do not be deceived, O king, for this is clay inside and bronze outside, and it has never eaten or drunk anything."

And the king grew angry, and he called his priests and said to them, "If you do not tell me who eats these great provisions, you shall die. But if you show me that Bel eats them, Daniel shall die, because he is a blasphemer."
And Daniel said to the king, "Let it be according to your word."
And the priests of Bel were seventy, besides their wives and children. And the king went with Daniel to the house of Bel.
And the priests of Bel said, "Behold, we will now go outside; and you, O king, set out the food and mix the wine; set it out, and lock the door, and seal it with your seal.
And come in the morning: if you do not find that everything has been eaten by Bel, let us die, or else Daniel, who has spoken falsely against us."
But they made light of it, for they had made a hidden entrance under the table, and through it they would always go in and eat the food.

And when they had gone out from there, the king set out the food for Bel. And Daniel commanded his servants, and they brought ashes and sifted them in the presence of the king; and they went out and shut the door, and sealed it with the king's seal, and departed.
But the priests came in by night, as they were accustomed, with their wives and their children, and they ate everything and drank the wine.
And the king rose early in the morning, and Daniel with him.
And the king said, "Are the seals intact, Daniel?" And Daniel said, "They are intact, O king."
And as soon as they had opened the doors, the king looked at the table, and cried out with a loud voice and said, "Great are you, O Bel, and there is no deceit with you, not even one!"
Daniel laughed, and held the king back so that he would not go in, and said, "Look now at the floor, and find out whose footprints these are."
And the king said, "I see here the footprints of men and of women and of children."

And when he saw this, the king grew angry, and he seized the priests and their wives and their children; and they showed him the secret doors through which they used to go in and eat what was set out on the table.
And the king put them to death, and gave Daniel authority over Bel; and he destroyed it and tore down its temple.
And there was a great dragon in that same place, and the Babylonians served it.
And the king said to Daniel, "Behold, now you cannot say that this is not a living god; so come and worship it."
And Daniel said, "I will worship the Lord my God, for he is the living God."
"But you, O king, give me authority, and I will kill this dragon without sword or staff [?]." And the king said, "I give it to you."
And Daniel took pitch and fat and hair, and boiled them together, and made them into round lumps, and threw them into the dragon's mouth, and the dragon burst open.

And Daniel said, "Now see the things you worship!" And when the Babylonians heard it, they grew very angry, and they gathered against the king and said, "The king has become a Jew. He has destroyed Bel and killed the dragon, and he has slaughtered the priests."
And they said to the king, "Give us Daniel. Otherwise we will kill you and plunder your whole house."
And the king saw that they were pressing him hard, and he was forced against his will, and he handed Daniel over to them.
And they threw him into the lions' pit, and he was there six days.
There were seven lions in the pit, and every day they were given two human bodies and two sheep [?]. But now they were given nothing, so that they would eat Daniel.
Now the prophet Habakkuk was in Judea. He had made a stew, broken bread into it, and put it in a bowl, and he was going out into the field to take it to the reapers.
And the angel of the Lord said to Habakkuk, "Take the meal you have to Babylon, to Daniel in the lions' den."
And Habakkuk said, "Lord, I have never seen Babylon, and I do not know the den."
And the angel of the Lord took hold of the hair of his head and lifted him up by the hair of his crown with the swiftness of his spirit, and set him down in Babylon at the den.
And Habakkuk called out and said, "Daniel, Daniel, take this food which the Lord has sent you."
And Daniel said, "For you have remembered me, O Lord, and you do not forsake those who love you."
And Daniel got up and ate. And the angel of the Lord at once brought Habakkuk back to his own place.
On the seventh day the king came to mourn for Daniel. He came to the den and looked in, and he saw Daniel sitting there.
And the king cried out in a loud voice and said, "Great are you, O Lord God of Daniel, and there is no other god besides you."
And they pulled Daniel up out of the den. And the king threw into the den those who were guilty of trying to destroy him, and the lions ate them at once before his eyes.
